clue.text: Cooler manner shown by Secretary of State running into Queen

parts.note: an air is a manner or bearing
Condi is Condoleezza Rice, US Secretary of State when the puzzle appeared

indicators.note: running suggests the letters of the word into are set loose and rearranged

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A US Secretary of State's cool demeanour as she bumps into the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' makes TION from the letters of 'into'; 'shown by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An air conditioner is a machine that cools a room, so it is a cooler.

clue.text: It can appear odd to Christian man, being a Republican

indicators.note: odd suggests the words to Christian man appear in a strange new arrangement

explanation.surface: Becoming a republican might look strange to a Christian man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It can appear' and 'being a' are link words around the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A republican in the British sense opposes the monarchy, so is against kings and queens.

clue.text: King's joint occupation fosters ill-feeling

indicators.note: occupation means one piece occupies, or sits inside, the other

parts.note: R (Rex) for king, with the S of the possessive
the ankle is a joint of the leg

explanation.surface: Sharing an occupied land with the King breeds resentment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'King's' gives R plus S, and 'occupation' has ANKLE sitting between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rankles keeps causing bitterness or resentment, fostering ill-feeling.

clue.text: British and US?

parts.note: read as the speaker saying 'we British' and naming 'us' as a group, the phrase asks for the reflexive pronoun meaning us

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Britain and the United States; read 'US' as the pronoun us.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is the emphatic or reflexive form of us, a group including the speaker.

clue.text: Some confusion in boy turning up as girl

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
in a down clue, turning up reads the word upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: confusion means the letters of some are jumbled

explanation.surface: A muddled boy shows up dressed as a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses LAD, and 'confusion' jumbles 'Some'; DAMOSEL is an old poetic spelling of damsel.
explanation.definitionFit: Damosel is an archaic, poetic form of damsel, a young unmarried girl.

clue.text: Vessel said to test soldiers

indicators.note: said to indicates the words are to be heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: test means try, and soldiers are RM, the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A boat is reputedly used to put troops through their paces.
explanation.walkthrough: TRY plus RM spoken as 'try ar-em' sounds like the ancient ship; RM, the Royal Marines, are British soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A trireme was an ancient Greek or Roman warship with three banks of oars, a vessel.

clue.text: Rise of Communist Party is comparatively unusual

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the pieces upwards, so the whole run is backwards

parts.note: a red is a communist
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A communist party's rise counts as something of a rarity.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading RED DO upwards gives the answer; the grid's ORDER is a slip for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Odder is the comparative of odd, which means strange or unusual.

clue.text: Former dictator found in River Test

indicators.note: found in means one piece is discovered inside the other

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
Idi Amin was Uganda's dictator in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A deposed tyrant turns up in the River Test, a Hampshire chalk stream.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a real English river, so 'River Test' looks like one name, but 'Test' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine someone or something is to test or inspect them closely.

clue.text: Part of the Light Brigade?

parts.note: the famous Charge of the Light Brigade suggests a cavalryman, but read light as electric power and a brigade member as something that charges cells

explanation.walkthrough: The Charge of the Light Brigade was a doomed British cavalry attack in the Crimean War.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery charger restores power to cells that run lights, a punning member of a light brigade.

clue.text: Grass instrument?

parts.note: Grass is the German novelist Günter Grass, and his famous novel is named after a child's percussion toy

explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a plant, as in a reed; it is the author.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tin Drum is Günter Grass's 1959 novel, its title naming a toy percussion instrument.

clue.text: State takes in goddess

parts.note: Diana is the Roman goddess of hunting

explanation.surface: A country welcomes a goddess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link: IN is simply followed by DIANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Indiana is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Film director of note takes in everything

indicators.note: takes in means one piece swallows the other

parts.note: me (or mi) is a note in the sol-fa scale
all means everything

explanation.surface: A notable film-maker takes in everything around him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' looks like 'famous'; 'note' gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Malle was a French film director, maker of Au revoir les enfants.

clue.text: Toss of spare coin may provide something to chew

indicators.note: a toss throws the letters of spare about into a new order

parts.note: to mint is to coin money

explanation.surface: Flipping a spare coin might win you some gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toss of' rearranges 'spare' to SPEAR; 'may provide' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a mint flavour used in chewing gum, so something to chew.

clue.text: Chamberlain remains in place of Europe in America

indicators.note: in place of means one piece replaces another

parts.note: Neville Chamberlain was British Prime Minister before the Second World War
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Chamberlain's remains lie somewhere other than Europe, in America.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the E of NEVILLE for ASH; the definition is loose, a place found in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Nashville, Tennessee, is a city in the USA, famous for country music.

clue.text: Shakespearean pursuer

parts.note: recalls the stage direction in The Winter's Tale, 'Exit, pursued by' an animal

explanation.definitionFit: In The Winter's Tale Antigonus leaves the stage chased by an animal, the play's famous pursuer.

clue.text: Goddess tied Harpo in knots

indicators.note: in knots suggests the letters of tied Harpo are tangled up

explanation.surface: A goddess has tied the Marx brother Harpo up in knots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in knots' scrambles 'tied Harpo'; Harpo was the silent Marx brother.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphrodite is the Greek goddess of love and beauty.

clue.text: Grass instruments

definitions.meaning: reed instruments such as oboes and clarinets are called by this name

explanation.walkthrough: This echoes 9-across, where 'Grass instrument' meant something quite different.
explanation.definitionFit: Reeds are both water grasses and the woodwind instruments sounded by a vibrating reed.

clue.text: Fade away, rather like a Welshman?

parts.note: Evan is a typical Welsh man's name
the suffix -ish means rather like

explanation.surface: Vanishing is a typically Welsh thing to do, it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as EVAN-ISH, like an Evan.
explanation.definitionFit: Evanish is a poetic word meaning to vanish or fade away.

clue.text: Drunk hit copper, knowing what would happen later

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of hit copper are reeling into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunk who struck a policeman knew trouble was coming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the person; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A prophetic person foretells events, knowing what is to come.

clue.text: Flourish of Carmen's creator

definitions.meaning: to flourish is to thrive or do well
... Mérimée wrote the novella Carmen, on which Bizet's opera is based

explanation.walkthrough: 'Carmen' makes one think of Bizet, but the opera came from Mérimée's story.
explanation.definitionFit: To prosper is to thrive; Prosper Mérimée, author of the novella Carmen, is the second sense.

clue.text: Where to find a Republican?

parts.note: points to the clue numbered 1 in the down list, whose answer means a republican

explanation.walkthrough: A self-referential clue: look at 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The entry at 1 down in this grid is a word meaning a republican, so that is where one is found.

clue.text: Standing of French Queen and significantly smaller

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up reads the pieces from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: reine is French for queen
et is French for and

explanation.surface: The status of a French queen, much reduced in size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' governs both 'Queen' and 'and'; 'Standing' turns REINEET upwards; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenier is the comparative of teeny, tiny, so it means appreciably smaller.

clue.text: Principal's manner of speaking betokens a grave situation

parts.note: a principal is a head teacher, with the possessive S
tone is the manner or quality of one's voice

explanation.surface: The principal's tone of voice signals that things are serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'betokens' is a link; 'a grave situation' means the site of a grave, not a serious state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstone is the stone set up to mark where a grave is situated.

clue.text: Jack's raised protuberances

definitions.note: Jack Straw, British Foreign Secretary at the time; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: in a down clue raised reads the word from the bottom up

parts.note: warts are small lumpy protuberances on the skin

explanation.surface: Jack has some raised lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Straw was the British Foreign Secretary when the puzzle appeared; 'Jack's' is 'Jack is', the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname completes the name of Jack Straw, a well-known British politician.

clue.text: Last appearance in a home game …

indicators.note: appearance in says the answer appears inside the run of words a home game

explanation.surface: A team's final outing is at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the next clue's rugby surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the last letter of the Greek alphabet, hence the last of anything.

clue.text: … rugby trips can go wrong — one might put one's foot in it

definitions.text: one might put one's foot in it

indicators.note: go wrong suggests the letters are out of their proper order

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union

explanation.surface: Rugby tours can end in disaster, someone making a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put one's foot in it' looks like making a blunder; it is meant literally, a rider's foot in a stirrup.
explanation.definitionFit: A stirrup is the loop a horse rider puts a foot into.

clue.text: Supposing love leads to languishing?

parts.note: love is zero, O, in tennis scoring, and leads to puts it at the front
pining means languishing or wasting away

explanation.surface: Does falling in love make a person pine?
explanation.walkthrough: 'leads to' is a link here, saying O comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold an opinion, so opining is supposing or believing.

clue.text: Earth won't shake with blunder by Bush

indicators.note: shake means the letters of Earth won't are shaken up

parts.note: an error is a blunder

explanation.surface: The world won't be shaken by another of Bush's mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shake' rearranges 'Earth won't' to THEWARONT; 'with' is a link. The definition is loose: the campaign waged by President Bush.
explanation.definitionFit: George W. Bush launched the campaign against terrorism after the September 2001 attacks.
